transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess my wife thought it might be good for me to talk to someone. I’ve been working on a memorial for my brother, and it’s… gotten a little bigger than I first planned. I mean, I think it’s a good thing, honoring him and all, but I’ve been spending most days tracking down songs, calling people, planning displays, even thinking through trips for it.

My wife says I’ve kind of let the garden and my walking group and, well, most everything else slide. I don’t mean to make it sound too dramatic. I’m just trying to do it right, you know?
While you’ve been working on the memorial, have you felt unusually high or euphoric?

I wouldn’t say “euphoric” exactly… that sounds a little much. But yes, there are moments where I feel sort of lit up, like I’ve got this real purpose, like if I get it right the whole town will finally understand what my brother meant to our family.

And then… I guess I can get short with people. My wife, or someone at the senior center, if they slow things down or question part of the display. I’m not proud of that. I just feel like they don’t see how important it is. Does that make sense?
Since this started, have you been needing less sleep than usual?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think of it as “needing less sleep,” exactly. Some nights I’m up thinking about things for the memorial, but at my age sleep isn’t always perfect anyway, you know? I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
Have you had more energy than usual lately?

Maybe a bit, yes. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but I haven’t been sitting in my chair the way I used to.

I’m up hauling boxes, making calls, sorting and re-sorting papers, walking from one room to the next… it’s like once I get going, my body has more steam in it than I’d expect at my age. I suppose that counts as more energy, doesn’t it?
Have you felt more important or specially chosen than usual while working on the memorial?

Specially chosen… well, I don’t know if I’d put it that strongly, Doctor. I’m not trying to make myself out to be some important person.

But… there is something I’ve been a little hesitant to say, because it sounds odd. Those old ballads my brother kept — I don’t think they’re just songs. I’m pretty certain there are warnings tucked in them for me. Like certain words are meant to point me toward what I’m supposed to understand for the memorial.

My wife says I’m reading too much into it, and maybe that’s what it sounds like from the outside. But I know what I heard in those words. I’m explaining that all right, aren’t I?
Lately, have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

Depressed most of the day… no, I wouldn’t say that. I mean, I have my moments, of course, but not like I’m under a dark cloud all day or anything. I haven’t really noticed that as the main thing. Does that answer what you mean?
Has this been causing serious problems in your daily life?

Well… “serious” is a strong word, isn’t it? I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But yes, I suppose it has gotten in the way. I’ve missed my walking group and book club more than once, and the garden’s gone a bit wild because I keep putting everything into this memorial display. Some friends at the senior center have been… upset with me, I think, because every conversation turns back to it.

And my wife says our days have started revolving around calming me down or steering me away from another phone call, another trip, another argument. I don’t mean to be difficult. I’m just trying to get it right. But yes… I can see how that would count as causing problems.
Did these changes in your mood and behavior start only after your brother died?

Yes… I suppose that’s fair to say. It really began after my brother passed, when I started putting together his tribute.

It’s been about two months now. I didn’t think of it as a “change” at first — more like I was just trying to honor him properly — but looking back, yes, that’s when it started. Is that the kind of timeline you’re asking for?
Have your thoughts been racing lately?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if I’d call it “racing” exactly. It’s more that my mind keeps hopping around.

One minute I’m thinking about a display case, then suddenly I’m planning a road trip to track down a cousin, and then some line from an old ballad comes into my head. I try to write it all down in order, but I can’t seem to slow it enough to make it neat.

Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have these unusually energized and driven feelings been present nearly every day for at least a week?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been more than a week, certainly.

It’s really been going on about two months now, since my brother passed and I started working on his tribute. Maybe not every single moment of every day, but the driven feeling has been there nearly every day, I’d say. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you heard voices when no one was there?

I… yes, I suppose I have, though I don’t want it to sound worse than it is.

Sometimes when I’m at the kitchen table sorting through my brother’s song sheets, I’ll hear his voice just clear as day behind me — like he’s humming, or telling me which tune should come next. But when I turn around, there isn’t anyone there, and no one else in the house seems to hear it.

Is that what you mean by voices?

This makes bereavement-related adjustment disorder (F43.21) and depressive episode (F32.9) unlikely.
